newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Bank of Botswana approves dual stock listings.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Botswana approves dual stock listings.

text.p: The Bank of Botswana has relaxed capital account exchange controls to permit dual listings on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) of companies listed on other reputable stock exchanges anywhere in the world.
The move, described by the BSE as a major policy shift, will open up pula hedge investments to Botswana residents.
The purchase of shares in dual-listed companies will be regarded as domestic investments, tradeable in pula at current rates of exchange.

The local currency, indirectly linked to the South African rand, has been under pressure since the rand started a downward slide at the beginning of this year. The pula has lost 28 per cent against the sterling and 22 per cent against the U.S. dollar.
"Dual listing will dramatically enhance domestic investment opportunties," BSE chief executive Alan Norrie said. "The significance of this major policy move should not be under estimated."
The limit on individual foreign portfolio investments in Botswanan companies is also expected to be increased soon.
At present no single investor can own more than five percent of a local company, and collectively not more than 49 percent of the company may be owned by foreign portfolio investors.
The BSE's market capitalisation currently stands at 1.2 billion pula, with 12 companies listed.
Of those companies, five are 100 percent locally owned, another five 70 percent owned by foreign parent operations, one 60 percent and one 50 percent owned by foreign principals.
Norrie now has his sights on the dual listing of diamond giant De Beers, a 50 percent partner with the Botswana government in Debswana.
Debswana is responsible for 80 percent of the county's export revenues and a direct 40 percent of GDP.

There is one application for dual listing pending. The Regent Pacific Group's US$50 million Undervalued Assets Africa Fund, primary-listed on the Dublin Stock Exchange, has applied for dual listings on the BSE and the Nairobi Stock Exchange.
BSE spokesman Andrew Ashton said approval for Regent's BSE listing was now expected within a couple of weeks.
In terms of Regent's target asset portfolio, 2.5 percent of the fund will be invested in Botswana and 10.2 percent in Kenya.
